digest.component_or_area: codebase-wide comment rationalization across six subsystems
propositions: Six subsystem agents triaged 439 files in src/rebar to identify ~2033 lines of comments misplaced outside their taxonomy destinations (history to tickets, architecture to ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema).
Load-bearing comments documenting replay-compatibility, security invariants, anti-refactor warnings, and API facts must be retained verbatim or corrected in place, never relocated or deleted.

Verified-stale comments contradicting current code (e.g., deterministic floor P1-P9 vs actual P1-P11, inverted CLI flags, obsolete Anthropic constraints) must be corrected where they document live invariants.
Each shard produces a do_not_move list recording blocks that appear relocatable but are load-bearing; these lists are appended to .joe-janitor/tools.md to prevent future re-flagging.
Eight sites restate the same four-paragraph argument about idempotent transform ordering; this argument is consolidated into a single ADR with inline blocks collapsed to citations.
Net measured recovery across all six shards (changes 1542–1547) is ~85 lines, an output of the work, not a fixed target; no relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate.
